He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, and that building stood across the valley through the whole sermon. He spoke of heaven and earth passing away in front of a house Scripture says was built like the heavens and the earth, in a sermon that began with that house coming down.

When Jesus died the temple curtain tore from top to bottom. The way in was opened through his flesh.

Hebrews warned that God would shake not only earth but heaven, removing what was made, so that what cannot be shaken would remain.

None of this makes Genesis 1 about a building: God made the real sky and ground, and Moses built a copy. Good readers differ on how far “heaven and earth” in Matthew 24:35 points to the temple. Scholars far from preterism also see the temple as a model of the cosmos; the difference here is the timing, inside “this generation”.
Israel built heaven and earth
The covenant lawsuit: the tabernacle built in the words of creation, Jesus facing the temple as he spoke of heaven and earth passing, the curtain torn and the house fallen, and a city with no temple.
When Jesus said “heaven and earth will pass away” (Matthew 24:35), where was he sitting, and what was he looking at?

A psalm says God built his sanctuary like the high heavens and like the earth: a picture of the world God made, with God enthroned at its centre.

The end of the tabernacle story repeats the end of the creation story: finished, saw, blessed, the Sabbath, and then God's glory filling the house.
Read that way in Jesus' day
Josephus called the tabernacle an imitation of the world and the temple curtain an image of the universe. Hebrews calls the holy places copies and shadows of heavenly things.
Witnesses in a covenant lawsuit
Moses and the prophets called heaven and earth to witness against Israel when the covenant was broken.
Facing the temple

Jesus left the temple, foretold its fall, and sat on the Mount of Olives opposite it. There he said this generation would not pass until all these things happened, and that heaven and earth would pass away.
Torn, then fallen
At the cross the curtain tore from top to bottom; forty years later the house was gone. Hebrews had warned of a shaking of earth and heaven that would leave only what cannot be shaken.
The New Jerusalem is a cube like the Most Holy Place, and it has no temple: God and the Lamb are its temple, and God dwells with his people.
Curtain torn
Jesus dies; the way into the holy place is opened.
The house built like heaven and earth falls.

Most readers take “heaven and earth” in Matthew 24:35 as the created universe: Jesus' words outlast even the world itself. Some add that the verse contrasts the passing of creation, at the end, with the permanence of his word, and is not a description of the temple at all.

Whatever the phrase includes, Jesus spoke it facing a building Scripture says was built like the heavens and the earth, in a sermon that began with that building's fall. The copy fell in AD 70; the dwelling of God with his people remains.

This does not make Genesis 1 about a building, and readers differ on how far to press the temple meaning in Matthew 24:35. Scripture still promises a renewed creation at Christ's return (Romans 8:19-23; 2 Peter 3:13), as the creeds confess.
